column1: # 18장 말투 지시. 열: 조각 앞머리 → 지시(영어, 짧게). @scene 행은 장면 설명(장면 끝까지 모든 요청에 붙는다).
@scene 열 번째 편지는 해 질 녘에
column2: During the La Mercè festival week, Yuna stays in and reads Martí's short letters six to nine, each ending with a small line of love never named. Two envelopes are left. She tells Marc, a reserved locksmith of few words, she wants to read the tenth somewhere high; he answers with a place and a time. Quiet, expectant.

column1: 열 번째 편지는 해 질 녘에

column2: brief answer: a place and a time

Sunset at the Carmel bunkers, an old Civil War gun site where people now watch the sun go down over Barcelona. Marc explains the place plainly. Yuna reads Martí's tenth letter: his last, telling her grandmother he has loved her since the first day, and that the clock is finished, covered with a white sheet, waiting. Yuna cries openly and Marc holds her hand. Deeply moving, quiet.
calm, a little out of breath
plain explanation, looking at the city

column1: 마지막 줄은 소리 내어 읽을 수가

column2: After sunset at the bunkers, Marc reads the letter and rereads one line: the clock is covered with a white sheet. He realizes the tall thing under a sheet in his workshop's basement, which his father always called an old wardrobe, is a grandfather clock. They plan to go down with the key tomorrow. That night Yuna writes to her mother in Korea. Quiet, then a dawning discovery, then calm.

column1: «Lo he tapado con una sábana blanca».
column2: rereading the sentence slowly, something dawning on him
slow, thinking it through as he speaks

column1: Un reloj de pie. Y yo buscando

column2: plain, his hand raised above his head
